specStatements.text: Students should be able to explain that homeostasis is the regulation of the internal conditions of a cell or organism to maintain optimum conditions for function in response to internal and external changes.
Homeostasis maintains optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions.
In the human body, these include control of: blood glucose concentration; body temperature; water levels.
These automatic control systems may involve nervous responses or chemical responses.

All control systems include: cells called receptors, which detect stimuli (changes in the environment); coordination centres (such as the brain, spinal cord and pancreas) that receive and process information from receptors; effectors, muscles or glands, which bring about responses which restore optimum levels.

concepts.definition: The regulation of the internal conditions of a cell or organism to maintain optimum conditions for function, in response to internal and external changes.
A cell that detects a stimulus, which is a change in the environment.
A part of the body, such as the brain, spinal cord or pancreas, that receives and processes information from receptors.
A muscle or gland that brings about a response which restores the optimum level.

concepts.term: internal conditions controlled in the human body
concepts.definition: In the human body, the conditions controlled by homeostasis include blood glucose concentration, body temperature and water levels.

misconceptions.question: Does homeostasis hold the internal conditions of the body at exactly the same value?
misconceptions.correct: No. Internal conditions do change, and homeostasis regulates them so that they are restored to the optimum in response to internal and external changes.
misconceptions.misconception: The internal conditions of the body stay constant and do not change.
misconceptions.whyItArises: The word 'maintain', and graphs drawn as a flat line, lead students to picture a value that is held fixed rather than one that moves away from the optimum and is then brought back.
misconceptions.correction: Homeostasis is the regulation of the internal conditions of a cell or organism to maintain optimum conditions for function in response to internal and external changes; effectors bring about responses which restore optimum levels after a change has been detected.

misconceptions.question: Why does the human body control internal conditions such as body temperature?
misconceptions.correct: To maintain optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions.
misconceptions.misconception: The body controls its internal conditions so that the person feels comfortable.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Students meet temperature, thirst and hunger as feelings they experience, so they explain the control of these conditions in terms of how the body feels rather than in terms of what cells need.
misconceptions.correction: Homeostasis maintains optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions; the sensations a person feels are not the reason the conditions are regulated.

misconceptions.question: Do all automatic control systems in the body work by nervous responses?
misconceptions.correct: No. These automatic control systems may involve nervous responses or chemical responses.
misconceptions.misconception: Every automatic control system in the body works by nervous responses.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Automatic control is usually taught first using reflex examples, so students link anything automatic to nerve impulses and overlook chemical responses.
misconceptions.correction: These automatic control systems may involve nervous responses or chemical responses, for example a chemical response coordinated by the pancreas.

misconceptions.question: Which part of a control system brings about the response?
misconceptions.correct: The effectors, muscles or glands, bring about responses which restore optimum levels.
misconceptions.misconception: The response is brought about by the receptors or by the coordination centre.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Receptors and coordination centres are described first and are the parts students remember best, so they credit them with carrying out the response as well as with detecting and processing.
misconceptions.correction: Receptors detect stimuli, coordination centres receive and process information from receptors, and effectors, muscles or glands, bring about responses which restore optimum levels.

mcqs.stem: During exercise a person's body temperature rises above its optimum level. Why does the body respond to bring the temperature back down?

options.text: To make the person feel comfortable when hot
options.rationale: A student who believes internal conditions are controlled for comfort picks this. It is wrong because homeostasis maintains optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions, not a sensation.

options.text: To keep optimum conditions for enzyme action
options.rationale: Homeostasis maintains optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions, so a temperature above the optimum is corrected.

options.text: To stop the internal conditions from changing
options.rationale: A student who believes internal conditions do not change picks this. It is wrong because the temperature has already changed; homeostasis restores it to the optimum in response to that change.

options.text: To let the receptors bring about the cooling
options.rationale: A student who thinks receptors carry out the response picks this. It is wrong because receptors detect stimuli, while effectors, muscles or glands, bring about responses which restore optimum levels.

mcqs.stem: The pancreas releases a hormone that lowers a high blood glucose concentration. Which statement about this control system is correct?

options.text: A nervous response restores the optimum level
options.rationale: A student who believes every automatic control system works by nerve impulses picks this. It is wrong because the pancreas releases a hormone, so the response described is chemical.

options.text: A chemical response prevents the level changing
options.rationale: A student who believes internal conditions are held constant picks this. It is wrong because the blood glucose concentration has risen, and the control system restores it to the optimum.

options.text: A chemical response restores the optimum level
options.rationale: Automatic control systems may involve nervous responses or chemical responses; a hormone released by the pancreas is a chemical response, and the optimum blood glucose concentration is restored.

options.text: A receptor response restores the optimum level
options.rationale: A student who credits receptors with carrying out the response picks this. It is wrong because receptors detect stimuli, while effectors bring about responses which restore optimum levels.

mcqs.stem: A person becomes cold and begins to shiver. Which structure is acting as the effector in this control system?

options.text: the muscles that contract to make the body shiver
options.rationale: Effectors are muscles or glands which bring about responses which restore optimum levels; here muscles contract to produce shivering.

options.text: the receptors that detect the fall in temperature
options.rationale: A student who mixes up the parts of a control system picks the detecting cells. It is wrong because receptors detect stimuli, changes in the environment, and do not bring about the response.

options.text: the brain that processes information from receptors
options.rationale: A student who thinks the coordination centre carries out the response picks the brain. It is wrong because the brain receives and processes information from receptors, while effectors bring about the response.

options.text: the nerves that carry impulses through the body
options.rationale: A student who believes control systems act only through nervous responses picks the nervous pathway. It is wrong because effectors are muscles or glands, not the pathway that carries information.
